TIL that humans are the best long-distance runners on the planet, able to beat horses (and everything else) in marathon distance races.
It goes back to hunting. Our prey could run faster but we would just track them.

Imagine you're an animal and you spot a hungry human, you would run as fast as you can, naturally. But eventually, you'll get tired. You'll collapse. Humans don't get tired, they're built for walking, they even carry food them to resupply themselves on the move. How must it feel knowing that no matter how far you run you can never escape? There's a reason humans are top of the food chain.
We're not the fastest and we certainly can't run very far at high speed. The reason we're on top of the food chain is our brain, nothing else.

That's why I said walking, not running like you're implying. Our bodies are built for walking and we can carry food and water with us to refuel, letting us go on even longer.

Our brain is unlike anything else, but it wouldn't do much good with a weak physical interface.

As I recall, our brains really developed after we reached the apex of the food chain.

No doubt intelligence was a factor, but so were size, strength, endurance, and dexterity.

It took a lot of attributes to win on this planet.

I remember watching on a BBC documentary I think planet earth, a tribesman chased a buffalo until it died from exhaustion. He then sat with it during its last moments. Fascinating and moving. We are designed to cover long distances efficiently. Shame what the human race has become.
Another fascinating show on Netflix is Decoding Neanderthals. It may still be there, may not be, but it was interesting to see how innovative our ancestors really were.

This is slightly overstated as it's only true in some environments. For example, sled dogs outpace us in their cold environment.

For an interesting read, check out this skeptics.se question about it. It covers sled dogs and also talks about some of the horse vs. human marathons that haven't been as dominated by humans as you may believe.

Humans are still one of the fastest distance runners across all environments.
I recommend reading The Sports Gene by Dave Epstein for people interested in this. It's a fantastic book.
